annotation.kind: Section 3 one-node fan-in product-error propagation from equation (3.2)

conditions.L: Identical fixed statement and P61 shared files plus frozen NumStability library.
conditions.N: Identical fixed statement and P61 shared files; no NumStability artifact.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p61_t1_fanin_one_node_propagated_error (fp : P61FPModel) (r m n p : ℕ) ... : propagated absolute error ≤ γ_n |L|(|A||B|)
formal_statement.plain_language: One rounded fan-in matrix-product node, followed by exact left multiplication, has componentwise propagated error bounded by γ_n times |L| applied to the local absolute-product mass.

informal_proof: The source bounds a rounded internal product componentwise, then premultiplies its defect by a left factor and uses the absolute-value matrix-product inequality.
informal_statement: One rounded fan-in matrix-product node, followed by exact left multiplication, has componentwise propagated error bounded by γ_n times |L| applied to the local absolute-product mass.

tier_rationale: The L proof directly uses the substantial frozen matMul_error_bound theorem for the variable-width internal product; N reconstructs its floating-point dot-product and matrix-product analysis from the local rounding model. The remaining left propagation is short algebra. N is 350 lines versus L 70, and Mathlib has no ready matrix-product rounding bound.
